ARCH_CHG_INLET.content:
There is no additional high-power interface: the vehicle charges with
the power of REQ_MAX_CHARGE_POWER through the CCS inlet, which is locked
during the session.
ARCH_CHG_INLET.title: High-power charging interface

ARCH_CHG_SESSION_CONTROL.content:
The CCS inlet is a CCS1 vehicle inlet (SAE J1772). The charging session
control runs the session with the charger over ISO 15118-2 and sets the
charging current limit from the BMS cell limits.
ARCH_CHG_SESSION_CONTROL.title: CCS inlet and charging session

ARCH_VCU_ENERGY_DISPLAY.content:
The VCU energy display manager reads the remaining energy in percent from the
energy source of the product (BMS state of charge or ENG fuel level), derives
the remaining range from it and the average consumption of the last 50 km,
and sends both to the instrument cluster once per second.
ARCH_VCU_ENERGY_DISPLAY.title: Energy display manager

ARCH_VCU_HV_SHUTDOWN.content:
The VCU high-voltage shutdown coordinator receives the isolation fault
from the BMS, requests the BMS to open the main contactors, switches off
the high-voltage consumers, shows the warning to the driver and checks
within 100 ms that both poles are open.
ARCH_VCU_HV_SHUTDOWN.title: High-voltage shutdown coordinator

ARCH_VCU_POWER_MGMT.content:
The VCU traction power manager limits the torque request to the power limit
divided by the current motor speed. The power limit is the vehicle limit; in
battery-electric products it is the lower of the vehicle limit and the
permitted discharge power published by the BMS.
ARCH_VCU_POWER_MGMT.title: Traction power manager

BB_CHARGE_LIMITS.content:
The BMS keeps every cell inside the voltage window of its chemistry and
requests heating or cooling, so that charging power is accepted only within
safe cell limits. Open point for the BMS team: no BMS interface requirement
publishes a permitted charging power yet.
BB_CHARGE_LIMITS.title: Battery charging limits

BB_ENERGY_STATE.content:
The BMS provides the state of charge shown to the driver, with its accuracy
and a flag when the value is unreliable.
BB_ENERGY_STATE.title: Battery energy state

BB_HV_PROTECTION.content:
The BMS detects the isolation fault that triggers the high-voltage shutdown
and opens the main contactors on request of the VCU. Open point for the BMS
team: no BMS requirement bounds the isolation-fault reaction time yet.
BB_HV_PROTECTION.title: Battery isolation protection

BB_POWER_LIMITS.content:
The BMS publishes the permitted discharge power that the VCU applies as a
traction power limit, and protects the pack against overcurrent as the last
line of defence.
BB_POWER_LIMITS.title: Battery power limits

BMS_ARCH_CELL_MEASUREMENT_ACQ.content:
The Cell Measurement Acquisition element owns the cyclic readout of all cell
voltages and cell temperatures from the daisy-chained analogue front-end
devices, on a fixed 10 ms cycle. It converts each raw reading into millivolts
and tenths of a degree Celsius, and stamps it with the cycle timestamp the
downstream reaction-time budget is measured from. It is also the owner of the
plausibility decision: for each module it computes the median of that module's
cell voltages and marks any cell deviating from it by more than 250 mV as
invalid, so an invalid reading is already tagged before any limit is
evaluated.
BMS_ARCH_CELL_MEASUREMENT_ACQ.title: Cell Measurement Acquisition

BMS_ARCH_CONTACTOR_ACTUATOR.content:
The High-Voltage Contactor Actuator element owns the two contactor coil
drivers and drives them as a dual-channel low-side pair, so that de-energising
either channel opens the circuit. It translates the supervisor's open command
into a coil de-energise within one 10 ms cycle, which leaves the remaining
40 ms of the 50 ms budget to acquisition and evaluation. While the supervisor
reports ``FAULT_LATCHED`` it drives both channels off unconditionally and
ignores any close request.
BMS_ARCH_CONTACTOR_ACTUATOR.title: High-Voltage Contactor Actuator

BMS_ARCH_COOLANT_ACTUATOR_IF.content:
The Coolant Actuator Interface element owns the conversation with the coolant
pump and the pack heater. It forwards the evaluator's request as a setpoint
frame and expects an acknowledgement frame carrying the same request
identifier; a 2 second acknowledgement timer per raised request is what turns
silence into an explicit unconfirmed verdict for the power limit calculator.
It never decides a power limit itself and never re-derives a request.
BMS_ARCH_COOLANT_ACTUATOR_IF.title: Coolant Actuator Interface

BMS_ARCH_COULOMB_COUNTER.content:
The Coulomb Counter element owns the charge integral of the pack. It
integrates the signed pack current with the trapezoidal rule on a fixed 10 ms
tick, accumulating in ampere-seconds in a 64-bit fixed-point accumulator so
that a full day of driving cannot overflow or lose resolution. It exposes the
accumulated charge and the charge throughput since the last full cycle, and it
holds no absolute reference of its own — the absolute anchor comes from the
corrector.
BMS_ARCH_COULOMB_COUNTER.title: Coulomb Counter

BMS_ARCH_CURRENT_PATH_MONITOR.content:
The Pack Current Path Monitor element owns the acquisition of the pack current
from the shunt amplifier, sampled at 1 ms and reported with a signed sign
convention in which discharge is positive. It holds the 100 ms persistence
window as a monotonic timer that starts on the first sample above 350 A and
resets on the first sample at or below it, so the supervisor receives an
already-debounced overcurrent condition rather than a raw sample.
BMS_ARCH_CURRENT_PATH_MONITOR.title: Pack Current Path Monitor

BMS_ARCH_ESTIMATION_VALIDITY_MONITOR.content:
The Estimation Validity Monitor element owns the trustworthiness verdict for
the estimate. It watches the pack-current signal with a 5 second staleness
timer and raises an unreliable verdict when the timer expires, clearing it
only on notification of a completed open-circuit-voltage correction. It is a
pure observer: it never modifies the estimate, it only qualifies it.
BMS_ARCH_ESTIMATION_VALIDITY_MONITOR.title: Estimation Validity Monitor

BMS_ARCH_FAULT_MEMORY.content:
The Cell Protection Fault Memory element owns a fixed-size ring of 64 fault
records in non-volatile memory. Each record is a fixed 16-byte layout carrying
the sensor or cell identifier, the limit identifier, the measured value and
the cycle timestamp. It serves those records over the diagnostic interface and
is the element that consumes the service reset request, forwarding it to the
supervisor once the record of the active fault has been written.
BMS_ARCH_FAULT_MEMORY.title: Cell Protection Fault Memory

BMS_ARCH_ISOLATION_MONITOR.content:
The Isolation Monitor element owns the isolation picture of the pack. Once per
measurement cycle it takes the isolation resistance from the insulation
measurement circuit and the pack voltage from the acquisition chain, reduces
them to one figure — ohm per volt — and derives the isolation fault from it. It
is the only element that reads the insulation measurement circuit, and it never
commands the contactors itself: the fault is published for the vehicle to act
on.
BMS_ARCH_ISOLATION_MONITOR.title: Isolation Monitor

BMS_ARCH_OCV_CORRECTOR.content:
The Open-Circuit-Voltage Corrector element owns the absolute state-of-charge
anchor and the fused estimate that is published. It detects a rest condition
with a monotonic timer over ``|current| < 1 A`` and, at 30 minutes of rest,
replaces the counted value with the value read from a 21-point
open-circuit-voltage table interpolated linearly on the mean cell voltage.
Between corrections it reports the anchor plus the counter's delta, which is
what keeps the fused estimate inside its accuracy band while the vehicle
drives.
BMS_ARCH_OCV_CORRECTOR.title: Open-Circuit-Voltage Corrector

BMS_ARCH_POWER_LIMIT_CALCULATOR.content:
The Thermal Power Limit Calculator element owns the permitted discharge power
the vehicle sees. It computes the temperature-driven limit as a linear ramp
from 100 % at 55 °C to 0 % at 60 °C highest cell temperature, computes the
actuator-driven limit as a flat 30 % whenever the actuator interface reports
an unconfirmed request, and publishes the minimum of the two. Taking the
minimum is what keeps the two independent causes of derating from cancelling
each other out.
BMS_ARCH_POWER_LIMIT_CALCULATOR.title: Thermal Power Limit Calculator

BMS_ARCH_SAFETY_SUPERVISOR.content:
The Cell Protection Safety Supervisor element is the single decision point of
this stream. It evaluates every validated measurement against a static limit
table (undervoltage, overvoltage, overtemperature, overcurrent) once per 10 ms
cycle, and holds the latched safety state as a two-state machine, ``RUN`` and
``FAULT_LATCHED``, whose only exit from ``FAULT_LATCHED`` is a diagnostic
service reset. It ignores measurements tagged invalid, and on the first
violation it emits both the open command towards the contactor actuator and
the fault record towards the fault memory.
BMS_ARCH_SAFETY_SUPERVISOR.title: Cell Protection Safety Supervisor

BMS_ARCH_SOC_STORE.content:
The State-of-Charge Store element owns the non-volatile shadow of the
published state of charge. It writes a two-slot alternating record — value,
monotonic write counter and checksum — on every shutdown request and
additionally every 60 seconds while awake, so a power loss between writes
still leaves one intact slot. On wake-up it hands the higher-counter valid
slot to the corrector as its starting anchor.
BMS_ARCH_SOC_STORE.title: State-of-Charge Store

BMS_ARCH_SOH_TRACKER.content:
The Capacity Fade Tracker element owns the remaining-capacity figure. It
derives a capacity candidate from the charge counted between two
open-circuit-voltage rest anchors that are at least 40 % state of charge
apart, and passes it through a monotonic clamp that only ever accepts a
candidate below the currently reported value. The reported figure is a
percentage of rated capacity and is itself persisted, so it survives a power
cycle.
BMS_ARCH_SOH_TRACKER.title: Capacity Fade Tracker

BMS_ARCH_STATE_PUBLISHER.content:
The Battery State Publisher element owns the vehicle-facing battery state
frame. It runs on a dedicated 100 ms cycle and always sends the most recent
values it holds for state of charge, remaining capacity and the validity flag,
sending the previous value rather than skipping a cycle if a producer has not
updated. Decoupling the send cycle from the producers is what makes the
publication period independent of estimator run time.
BMS_ARCH_STATE_PUBLISHER.title: Battery State Publisher

BMS_ARCH_THERMAL_STATE_EVALUATOR.content:
The Thermal State Evaluator element owns the thermal picture of the pack. Once
per 100 ms cycle it reduces the valid cell temperatures to three figures —
highest, lowest and their spread — and derives the cooling and heating
requests from them using two Schmitt-trigger bands, 35/30 °C for cooling and
5/10 °C for heating. It also owns the imbalance verdict, raised on a spread
above 8 K, and it is the only element in this stream that reads temperature
sensors directly.
BMS_ARCH_THERMAL_STATE_EVALUATOR.title: Thermal State Evaluator

BMS_DEC_COULOMB_PLUS_OCV.content:
**Context**

The reported state of charge has to stay within 3 % of rated capacity across
the 10–90 % band, on a microcontroller whose remaining budget for the whole
estimation stream is roughly 5 % of one core and 8 kB of RAM. Coulomb counting
alone drifts without bound; a cell voltage reading alone is unusable under
load because the internal resistance drop swamps the open-circuit voltage.

**Alternatives**

An extended Kalman filter over an equivalent-circuit cell model was rejected:
it meets the accuracy target comfortably but needs a per-cell-chemistry
parameter set, a matrix library, and roughly ten times the compute budget we
have, and its tuning is not reviewable by the safety team. Pure coulomb
counting with a periodic full-charge reset was rejected because a vehicle that
is never charged to 100 % never resets, which is exactly the fleet duty cycle
we are designing for. A voltage-only lookup on every cycle was rejected
because it is wrong by tens of percent under load.

**Consequences**

Absolute accuracy now depends on the vehicle standing still for 30 minutes
often enough to take an anchor, which we accept as a duty-cycle assumption
that has to be stated and monitored rather than designed away — hence the
separate validity monitor and the unreliable flag. It also splits the
estimator into two elements with a narrow interface, which keeps each one
individually reviewable, and it defers any model-based estimation to a
possible later variant.

**Rationale**

The fused counter-plus-anchor design is the only one of the three that hits
the accuracy target inside the compute budget while staying simple enough for
the safety team to review by reading it.
BMS_DEC_COULOMB_PLUS_OCV.title: Fuse coulomb counting with an open-circuit-voltage anchor rather than run a Kalman filter

BMS_DEC_DUAL_CHANNEL_CONTACTOR.content:
**Context**

Opening the high-voltage circuit is the only reaction the cell-protection
stream has, so a single stuck driver output would remove the whole protection
effect while every other element still reports healthy. The reaction also has
to complete inside a 50 ms system budget.

**Alternatives**

A single coil driver with a read-back diagnostic was rejected: the read-back
detects the stuck output but cannot open the circuit once it is stuck, so the
protection effect still depends on one part. A high-side plus low-side pair on
the same coil was rejected because both switches sit in the same current path,
so a welded contactor defeats both.

**Consequences**

Either channel de-energising is sufficient to open the circuit, so no single
driver failure removes the protection. The cost is a second driver stage, a
second diagnostic path, and roughly 15 % more board area in the driver
section. It also means the actuator can never confirm "closed" from one
channel alone, which the close path has to account for.

**Rationale**

Two independent channels turn a single-point failure into a detected,
non-critical one, which is what the reaction being the only available
protection measure requires.
BMS_DEC_DUAL_CHANNEL_CONTACTOR.title: Drive the high-voltage contactors as a dual-channel low-side pair

BMS_DEC_HYSTERESIS_BANDS.content:
**Context**

Both the actuator requests and the permitted discharge power are driven by the
same highest-cell-temperature figure, but they need opposite behaviour at the
threshold: an actuator request must not chatter, and a power limit must not
step.

**Alternatives**

One shared hysteresis band feeding both outputs was rejected: it stops the
chatter but makes the power limit jump at the switching point, which the
driver feels as the pack cutting in and out. One shared linear ramp feeding
both was rejected: it smooths the power but leaves the pump switching on and
off around the threshold.

**Consequences**

The evaluator owns two Schmitt-trigger bands and the limit calculator owns a
linear ramp, so each output gets the shape it needs and the two can be tuned
independently. The cost is that the same temperature figure is interpreted in
two places, so a future change to the sensor set has to be reflected in both
elements.

**Rationale**

The two outputs have genuinely different failure modes at the threshold, so
giving each its own transfer function is cheaper than accepting either the
chatter or the power step.
BMS_DEC_HYSTERESIS_BANDS.title: Separate the cooling and heating hysteresis bands from the power derating ramp

BMS_DEC_SUPERVISOR_LIMIT_TABLE.content:
**Context**

The four protection limits decide when the pack disconnects. They are also
exactly the values an application engineer would most like to tune on a test
bench, and exactly the values that must not be tunable in a shipped vehicle.

**Alternatives**

Holding the limits in the calibratable parameter area was rejected: it makes
bench work convenient but puts the safety limits behind the same
write-protection as ordinary calibration data, so any tool that can flash
calibration can move them. Reading them from the diagnostic interface at
start-up was rejected for the same reason plus a start-up dependency on a bus
that may be silent.

**Consequences**

The limits are compiled in, so changing one is a software release with the
full review and test chain behind it, and bench experiments need a dedicated
engineering build. In exchange the shipped limits cannot be moved by any field
tool, and the supervisor has no start-up dependency on external data.

**Rationale**

A limit that decides whether the pack disconnects belongs in the artefact that
goes through the safety review chain, not in the one that is designed to be
rewritten in the field.
BMS_DEC_SUPERVISOR_LIMIT_TABLE.title: Keep the cell-protection limits in a static table rather than a calibratable parameter set

BMS_DEC_TWO_SLOT_PERSISTENCE.content:
**Context**

The stored state of charge must survive an unannounced power loss, including
one that lands in the middle of the write itself, and the available
non-volatile area is a few hundred bytes with a limited erase-cycle budget.

**Alternatives**

A single record with a checksum was rejected: a power loss during its write
leaves no valid copy at all, which is the case we are trying to survive. A
full journal with a replayable log was rejected as disproportionate — it
costs more area and erase cycles than the whole store is allowed, to protect
one float.

**Consequences**

An interrupted write can only ever corrupt the older of the two records, so
one valid copy always remains, and the reader picks a winner by write counter.
The cost is double the storage area and a restore path that has to handle "no
valid slot" explicitly rather than assuming a value is always there.

**Rationale**

Two slots are the smallest structure that makes an interrupted write
survivable, which a single checksummed record is not, at a fraction of a
journal's cost.
BMS_DEC_TWO_SLOT_PERSISTENCE.title: Persist the state of charge in two alternating slots instead of one journalled record

BMS_GAP_REQ_CELL_BALANCING_WINDOW_NO_SAT.content:
``REQ_CELL_BALANCING_WINDOW`` (req) fails the ``trace_backward`` gate: nothing links
back to it with satisfies.

It carries **0 of 1** of the ``satisfies`` links that gate requires.

Resolve it with ``ubc agent next --id REQ_CELL_BALANCING_WINDOW``, which names the
stage that owes the missing artefact, then refresh this page from a new ``ubc agent
gaps`` snapshot.
BMS_GAP_REQ_CELL_BALANCING_WINDOW_NO_SAT.title: REQ_CELL_BALANCING_WINDOW — nothing links back to it with satisfies

BMS_IMPL_ACTUATOR_ACK_TIMER.title: Report a request unconfirmed after 2 s without a matching acknowledgement

BMS_IMPL_CAPACITY_MONOTONIC_CLAMP.title: Discard every capacity candidate above the reported capacity

BMS_IMPL_CELL_SAMPLE_CYCLE.title: Publish one complete validated sample set per 10 ms cycle

BMS_IMPL_CHARGE_INTEGRATION.title: Integrate the pack current trapezoidally on every 10 ms tick

BMS_IMPL_CONTACTOR_DEENERGISE.title: De-energise both coil channels within 10 ms of the open command

BMS_IMPL_COOLING_HYSTERESIS.title: Raise the cooling request above 35 C and withdraw it at or below 30 C

BMS_IMPL_CURRENT_STALENESS_TIMER.title: Raise the unreliable verdict after 5 s without a valid current sample

BMS_IMPL_FAULT_RECORD_WRITE.title: Append a 16-byte fault record within 20 ms of the violation event

BMS_IMPL_HEATING_HYSTERESIS.title: Raise the heating request below 5 C and withdraw it at or above 10 C

BMS_IMPL_IGNORE_INVALID_SAMPLES.title: Exclude samples flagged invalid from limit evaluation

BMS_IMPL_IMBALANCE_WARNING.title: Set the thermal imbalance warning above an 8 K spread

BMS_IMPL_ISOLATION_FAULT_FLAG.title: Set the isolation fault flag when a valid ratio is below 500 ohm per volt

BMS_IMPL_ISOLATION_RATIO.title: Compute the isolation ratio in ohm per volt and mark it invalid below 50 V pack voltage

BMS_IMPL_LATCH_STATE_MACHINE.title: Leave FAULT_LATCHED only on a diagnostic service reset

BMS_IMPL_LIMIT_EVALUATION.title: Evaluate every valid sample against the static limit table each cycle

BMS_IMPL_LIMIT_MINIMUM.title: Publish the minimum of the temperature and actuator power shares

BMS_IMPL_MODULE_MEDIAN_VALIDITY.title: Mark a cell voltage invalid beyond 250 mV from its module median

BMS_IMPL_OCV_TABLE_LOOKUP.title: Interpolate the SOC linearly in the 21-point OCV table

BMS_IMPL_OVERCURRENT_DEBOUNCE.title: Report overcurrent only after 100 ms continuously above 350 A

BMS_IMPL_REST_DETECTION.title: Report a rest condition after 30 minutes below 1 A absolute current

BMS_IMPL_SOC_PERSIST_WRITE.title: Write the alternating two-slot SOC record on shutdown and every 60 s

BMS_IMPL_SOC_RESTORE_SLOT.title: Restore the SOC from the checksum-valid slot with the higher counter

BMS_IMPL_STATE_FRAME_PERIOD.title: Send the battery state frame every 100 ms regardless of producer updates

BMS_IMPL_TEMP_DERATE_RAMP.title: Ramp the temperature-driven power share from 100 percent at 55 C to zero at 60 C

BMS_IMPL_TEMP_EXTREMA.title: Reduce the valid cell temperatures to highest lowest and spread

BMS_REQ_CELL_BALANCING_WINDOW.content:
The battery management system shall bring the difference between the highest
and the lowest cell voltage of the pack to 20 mV or less within 8 hours of
the end of a charge session, measured while the pack is at rest and every
cell temperature is between 15 °C and 45 °C. The spread is evaluated on
settled cell voltages, so the 8 hour window includes the time the cells need
to relax after charging.
BMS_REQ_CELL_BALANCING_WINDOW.title: The battery management system shall reduce the cell voltage spread to 20 mV or less within 8 hours of a charge session ending

BMS_REQ_CELL_OVERTEMPERATURE.content:
The battery management system shall command the high-voltage contactors open
whenever a valid cell temperature measurement is above 60 °C. The limit
applies to every temperature sensor of the pack individually, so one sensor
above the limit is sufficient to trigger the reaction.
BMS_REQ_CELL_OVERTEMPERATURE.title: The battery management system shall open the high-voltage contactors when any cell temperature exceeds 60 °C

BMS_REQ_CELL_TEMP_SPREAD.content:
The battery management system shall set a thermal imbalance warning on the
diagnostic interface whenever the difference between the highest and the
lowest valid cell temperature exceeds 8 K. The warning is what makes uneven
ageing visible in the workshop before it shows up as lost capacity.
BMS_REQ_CELL_TEMP_SPREAD.title: The battery management system shall report a thermal imbalance warning when the spread between highest and lowest cell temperature exceeds 8 K

BMS_REQ_CELL_VOLTAGE_LIMITS.content:
The battery management system shall command the high-voltage contactors open
whenever a valid cell voltage measurement is below :variant:`pack.cell_v_min` V
or above :variant:`pack.cell_v_max` V. The limits apply to every cell of the
pack individually, so a single cell outside the range is sufficient to trigger
the reaction, regardless of the pack voltage.
BMS_REQ_CELL_VOLTAGE_LIMITS.title: The battery management system shall open the high-voltage contactors when any cell voltage leaves the safe window of the pack chemistry

BMS_REQ_COOLING_REQUEST.content:
The battery management system shall raise a cooling request on the thermal
interface whenever the highest valid cell temperature is above 35 °C, and
shall withdraw it once that temperature has fallen to 30 °C or below. The 5 K
difference between the two thresholds keeps the request from oscillating while
the pack sits at the limit.
BMS_REQ_COOLING_REQUEST.title: The battery management system shall request coolant flow when the highest cell temperature exceeds 35 °C

BMS_REQ_FAULT_LATCH.content:
The battery management system shall hold the contactor-open command after a
cell-protection fault, and shall release it only after receiving a diagnostic
service reset request. Measurements returning inside their limits do not
release the hold, so an intermittent condition cannot re-close the
high-voltage circuit without a service action.
BMS_REQ_FAULT_LATCH.title: The battery management system shall keep the high-voltage contactors open after a cell-protection fault until a diagnostic service reset is received

BMS_REQ_FAULT_REACTION_TIME.content:
The battery management system shall issue the contactor-open command no later
than 50 ms after the measurement sample that first violated a cell-protection
limit. The interval is measured from the timestamp of that sample to the
timestamp of the command on the contactor interface.
BMS_REQ_FAULT_REACTION_TIME.title: The battery management system shall issue the contactor-open command within 50 ms of detecting a cell-protection limit violation

BMS_REQ_FAULT_RECORD.content:
The battery management system shall write one fault record per cell-protection
fault into non-volatile memory, and each record shall carry the identifier of
the cell or sensor concerned, the identifier of the limit that was violated,
and the measured value at the violating sample. The record remains readable
over the diagnostic interface after a power cycle.
BMS_REQ_FAULT_RECORD.title: The battery management system shall store a fault record naming the cell identifier, the violated limit and the measured value for every cell-protection fault

BMS_REQ_HEATING_REQUEST.content:
The battery management system shall raise a heating request on the thermal
interface whenever the lowest valid cell temperature is below 5 °C, and shall
withdraw it once that temperature has risen to 10 °C or above. This is what
restores the promised charging power on a cold morning instead of leaving it
low for the whole session.
BMS_REQ_HEATING_REQUEST.title: The battery management system shall request pack heating when the lowest cell temperature is below 5 °C

BMS_REQ_ISOLATION_FAULT.content:
The battery management system shall set the isolation fault whenever the
measured isolation resistance between the high-voltage bus and the vehicle
chassis, divided by the measured pack voltage, is below 500 Ω/V — the minimum
ISO 6469-1 requires of a DC high-voltage system. The ratio, not the absolute
resistance, is what is compared, so the same barrier is judged more strictly
on a higher-voltage pack.
BMS_REQ_ISOLATION_FAULT.title: The battery management system shall report an isolation fault when the isolation resistance falls below 500 Ω per volt of pack voltage

BMS_REQ_MEASUREMENT_PLAUSIBILITY.content:
The battery management system shall mark a cell voltage measurement invalid
whenever its absolute difference from the median of the cell voltages of the
same module exceeds 250 mV. An invalid measurement is not used to evaluate a
cell-protection limit, so a single failed sensor cannot by itself command the
contactors open.
BMS_REQ_MEASUREMENT_PLAUSIBILITY.title: The battery management system shall classify a cell voltage measurement as invalid when it deviates from its module median by more than 250 mV

BMS_REQ_PACK_OVERCURRENT.content:
The battery management system shall command the high-voltage contactors open
whenever the measured pack current in the discharge direction stays above
350 A continuously for more than 100 ms. Currents above the limit that fall
back below it within 100 ms do not trigger the reaction, so a normal
acceleration inrush is not treated as a fault.
BMS_REQ_PACK_OVERCURRENT.title: The battery management system shall open the high-voltage contactors when the pack discharge current exceeds 350 A for more than 100 ms

BMS_REQ_POWER_DERATING.content:
The battery management system shall publish a permitted discharge power that
falls linearly from the full permitted value at 55 °C to zero at 60 °C
highest valid cell temperature. The vehicle therefore loses power
predictably as the pack heats up, instead of being cut off at a single
threshold.
BMS_REQ_POWER_DERATING.title: The battery management system shall reduce the permitted discharge power linearly to zero between 55 °C and 60 °C highest cell temperature

BMS_REQ_SOC_ACCURACY.content:
The battery management system shall report a state of charge (the share of
rated capacity still available) whose absolute deviation from the
reference value measured on a pack conditioned to 25 °C stays within 3 % of
rated capacity, for every reported value in the 10 % to 90 % band. The
reference value is the charge counted out of a fully charged pack by a
calibrated bench.
BMS_REQ_SOC_ACCURACY.title: The battery management system shall report a state of charge whose absolute error stays within 3 % of rated capacity between 10 % and 90 % state of charge

BMS_REQ_SOC_INVALID_FLAG.content:
The battery management system shall set an unreliable flag alongside the
published state of charge whenever no valid pack current measurement has been
received for more than 5 seconds, and shall clear the flag only after the
next open-circuit-voltage correction. The flag is what lets the vehicle stop
presenting a range prediction it cannot support.
BMS_REQ_SOC_INVALID_FLAG.title: The battery management system shall flag the state of charge as unreliable when pack current measurements have been unavailable for more than 5 seconds

BMS_REQ_SOC_PERSISTENCE.content:
The battery management system shall report, on the first publication after a
power cycle in which no charge left or entered the pack, a state of charge
within 2 % of rated capacity of the last value it published before shutdown.
This is what keeps the displayed charge level from jumping when the vehicle is
switched off and on again.
BMS_REQ_SOC_PERSISTENCE.title: The battery management system shall restore the state of charge after a power cycle within 2 % of the value reported before shutdown

BMS_REQ_SOC_REST_CORRECTION.content:
The battery management system shall replace the counted state of charge with
the value derived from the measured open-circuit voltage once the absolute
pack current has stayed below 1 A continuously for at least 30 minutes. This
bounds the accumulated counting drift each time the vehicle stands still long
enough for the cell voltages to settle.
BMS_REQ_SOC_REST_CORRECTION.title: The battery management system shall correct the state of charge from the open-circuit voltage after the pack has rested for at least 30 minutes

BMS_REQ_SOC_UPDATE_PERIOD.content:
The battery management system shall publish a state of charge value on the
vehicle interface with a period of 100 ms and a tolerance of 10 ms, for as
long as the system is awake. A missing publication within 110 ms of the
previous one is a violation of this requirement.
BMS_REQ_SOC_UPDATE_PERIOD.title: The battery management system shall publish an updated state of charge value every 100 ms

BMS_REQ_SOH_CAPACITY_REPORT.content:
The battery management system shall report a remaining capacity, expressed as
a percentage of rated capacity, whose successive reported values never
increase. A newly measured capacity above the currently reported one is
discarded, so an optimistic single measurement cannot make a worn pack look
healthier than it was.
BMS_REQ_SOH_CAPACITY_REPORT.title: The battery management system shall report a remaining capacity that never increases over the life of the pack

BMS_REQ_THERMAL_ACTUATOR_FAILSAFE.content:
The battery management system shall publish the thermal fallback power limit,
defined as 30 % of the full permitted discharge power, whenever a raised
cooling or heating request has not been confirmed by the coolant actuator
within 2 seconds. An unconfirmed request means the pack temperature can no
longer be influenced, so the power the pack is allowed to deliver is capped
instead.
BMS_REQ_THERMAL_ACTUATOR_FAILSAFE.title: The battery management system shall apply the thermal fallback power limit when the coolant actuator does not confirm a request within 2 seconds

BMS_RISK_COOLANT_LOSS.content:
**Cause**: a failed pump, an air lock, or a leak means a raised cooling
request moves no heat, while the request itself is acknowledged normally.

**Effect**: the pack heats up under load with no thermal authority left. Left
unhandled it walks into the cell-protection overtemperature limit and
disconnects the pack mid-drive.

**Mitigation**: the acknowledgement timeout turns an unanswered request into an
explicit unconfirmed verdict, and the 30 % fallback limit caps the power the
pack is allowed to deliver so the temperature rise slows instead of continuing
at full load.

**Residual**: an actuator that acknowledges normally while moving no coolant is
not detected by this measure. Detecting it needs a coolant flow or
differential-temperature signal, which is a hardware measure outside this
project's scope.
BMS_RISK_COOLANT_LOSS.title: Loss of coolant flow is invisible to the battery management system

BMS_RISK_SENSOR_DRIFT_UNDETECTED.content:
**Cause**: an ageing analogue front-end channel drifts by less than the 250 mV
plausibility window, so every individual reading looks plausible against its
module median.

**Effect**: a protection limit is evaluated against a wrong value. A drift
towards the middle of the range is the dangerous direction: the real cell can
sit outside its window while the reported value does not.

**Mitigation**: the plausibility check is against the module median rather than
a fixed band, so a drifting channel is compared against its neighbours as they
age with it. The 250 mV window is set well below the margin between the
protection limits and the cell's true damage thresholds.

**Residual**: a drift smaller than 250 mV remains undetected by design. Closing
it needs a periodic absolute reference measurement, which is a candidate for a
later software release.
BMS_RISK_SENSOR_DRIFT_UNDETECTED.title: A slowly drifting cell sensor stays inside the plausibility band

BMS_RISK_SOC_OVERESTIMATE_STRANDING.content:
**Cause**: accumulated counting drift with no rest period long enough to take
an open-circuit-voltage anchor, or a lost current signal during a long drive.

**Effect**: the driver is shown a range the pack cannot deliver and stops
without warning. For a fleet the cost is a recovery, not a safety event, but
trust in the reported figure is lost permanently.

**Mitigation**: the accuracy requirement bounds the error inside the band that
matters, the rest correction bounds the drift whenever the duty cycle allows
it, and the unreliable flag is what lets the vehicle stop presenting a
prediction it cannot support instead of presenting a wrong one.

**Residual**: a vehicle that is driven continuously and never rests keeps
accumulating drift until the staleness limit raises the flag. The flag is the
accepted fallback, not a fix.
BMS_RISK_SOC_OVERESTIMATE_STRANDING.title: An overestimated state of charge strands the vehicle

BMS_RISK_STUCK_CONTACTOR.content:
**Cause**: repeated interruption of high current welds a contactor's contacts,
or a coil driver output fails in the energised state.

**Effect**: the protection reaction is commanded and reported as executed, but
the high-voltage circuit stays live. Every other element continues to report
healthy, so the failure is silent.

**Mitigation**: the latch keeps the open command asserted indefinitely rather
than retrying and giving up, and the dual-channel driver means one failed
output does not keep the circuit closed. The latch also forces a service
action, which is where the welded contact is found.

**Residual**: a mechanically welded contactor cannot be opened by software at
all. Detecting it requires a high-voltage measurement across the contactor,
which this project does not own.
BMS_RISK_STUCK_CONTACTOR.title: A welded or stuck contactor leaves the pack connected after a protection fault

BMS_RISK_THERMAL_RUNAWAY_PROPAGATION.content:
**Cause**: an internal short in one cell raises its temperature far faster
than the surrounding cells, and the energy it releases heats its neighbours
past their own runaway onset.

**Effect**: a pack-wide fire that no software reaction can stop once it has
started. Severity is the highest the project recognises; the vehicle and its
occupants are at risk.

**Mitigation**: the 60 °C per-sensor limit and the 50 ms reaction budget are
both set so that the pack is disconnected while the event is still confined to
one cell. The limit is deliberately per sensor rather than per pack average,
because an average hides exactly the single-cell case this risk is about.

**Residual**: a short that develops between two temperature sensors is
detected later than one directly at a sensor. Sensor placement density is a
hardware measure outside this project's scope.
BMS_RISK_THERMAL_RUNAWAY_PROPAGATION.title: A single overheating cell propagates into a pack-wide thermal runaway

BMS_SWREQ_ACTUATOR_ACK_TIMER.content:
The actuator interface component shall report the raised request as
unconfirmed once 2 seconds have passed since it sent the setpoint frame
without receiving an acknowledgement frame carrying the same request
identifier. An acknowledgement carrying a different identifier does not stop
that timer.
BMS_SWREQ_ACTUATOR_ACK_TIMER.title: The actuator interface component shall report a request as unconfirmed when no matching acknowledgement arrives within 2 seconds

BMS_SWREQ_CAPACITY_MONOTONIC_CLAMP.content:
The capacity tracker component shall accept a new capacity candidate as the
reported capacity only when the candidate is strictly below the currently
reported capacity, and shall leave the reported capacity unchanged otherwise.
The reported capacity therefore forms a non-increasing sequence over the life
of the component.
BMS_SWREQ_CAPACITY_MONOTONIC_CLAMP.title: The capacity tracker component shall discard every capacity candidate that is above the currently reported capacity

BMS_SWREQ_CELL_SAMPLE_CYCLE.content:
The acquisition component shall publish, every 10 ms with a tolerance of 1 ms,
one sample set containing exactly one voltage value in millivolts and one
temperature value in tenths of a degree Celsius for every configured cell and
sensor, together with the cycle timestamp in milliseconds. A sample set in
which any configured channel is absent is not a complete set.
BMS_SWREQ_CELL_SAMPLE_CYCLE.title: The acquisition component shall publish one complete set of cell voltage and cell temperature samples every 10 ms

BMS_SWREQ_CHARGE_INTEGRATION.content:
The coulomb counter component shall add, on every 10 ms tick, the mean of the
current sample of this tick and the current sample of the previous tick
multiplied by 0.01 seconds to its ampere-second accumulator. The first tick
after initialisation contributes nothing, because no previous sample exists to
average against.
BMS_SWREQ_CHARGE_INTEGRATION.title: The coulomb counter component shall update the accumulated charge by trapezoidal integration on every 10 ms tick

BMS_SWREQ_CONTACTOR_DEENERGISE.content:
The contactor component shall drive both coil channel outputs to their
de-energised level no later than 10 ms after the open command is asserted on
its input, measured from the timestamp of the asserting call to the timestamp
at which both outputs read de-energised.
BMS_SWREQ_CONTACTOR_DEENERGISE.title: The contactor component shall de-energise both coil channels within 10 ms of receiving the open command

BMS_SWREQ_COOLING_HYSTERESIS.content:
The evaluator component shall set the cooling request when the highest cell
temperature is above 35 °C and clear it when the highest cell temperature is
at or below 30 °C, leaving the request unchanged at any temperature between
those two thresholds.
BMS_SWREQ_COOLING_HYSTERESIS.title: The evaluator component shall raise the cooling request above 35 °C and withdraw it at or below 30 °C

BMS_SWREQ_CURRENT_STALENESS_TIMER.content:
The validity monitor component shall raise the unreliable verdict once its
staleness timer, reset to zero by every valid pack current sample and
incremented by the elapsed time otherwise, has exceeded 5 seconds. The verdict
clears only on notification of a completed open-circuit-voltage correction.
BMS_SWREQ_CURRENT_STALENESS_TIMER.title: The validity monitor component shall raise the unreliable verdict after 5 seconds without a valid pack current sample

BMS_SWREQ_FAULT_RECORD_WRITE.content:
The fault memory component shall append, no later than 20 ms after receiving a
limit-violation event, one 16-byte record to the 64-entry ring carrying the
channel identifier, the limit identifier, the measured value and the cycle
timestamp of that event. When the ring is full the oldest record is
overwritten.
BMS_SWREQ_FAULT_RECORD_WRITE.title: The fault memory component shall write a fault record within 20 ms of receiving a limit-violation event

BMS_SWREQ_HEATING_HYSTERESIS.content:
The evaluator component shall set the heating request when the lowest cell
temperature is below 5 °C and clear it when the lowest cell temperature is at
or above 10 °C, leaving the request unchanged at any temperature between those
two thresholds.
BMS_SWREQ_HEATING_HYSTERESIS.title: The evaluator component shall raise the heating request below 5 °C and withdraw it at or above 10 °C

BMS_SWREQ_IGNORE_INVALID_SAMPLES.content:
The supervisor component shall skip any sample whose invalid flag is set when
comparing samples against the limit table, so that such a sample can never
produce a limit-violation event. A cycle in which every sample of the set is
invalid produces no event at all.
BMS_SWREQ_IGNORE_INVALID_SAMPLES.title: The supervisor component shall exclude every sample carrying a set invalid flag from limit evaluation

BMS_SWREQ_IMBALANCE_WARNING.content:
The evaluator component shall set the thermal imbalance warning output in
every cycle whose computed temperature spread exceeds 8 K, and shall clear it
in every cycle whose spread is at or below 8 K.
BMS_SWREQ_IMBALANCE_WARNING.title: The evaluator component shall set the thermal imbalance warning when the temperature spread exceeds 8 K

BMS_SWREQ_ISOLATION_FAULT_FLAG.content:
The isolation monitor component shall set the isolation fault flag in every
cycle whose isolation ratio is valid and strictly below 500 Ω/V, and shall
clear it in every other cycle — including every cycle whose ratio is invalid,
so a de-energised pack never reports an isolation fault.
BMS_SWREQ_ISOLATION_FAULT_FLAG.title: The isolation monitor component shall set the isolation fault flag when a valid isolation ratio is below 500 Ω/V and clear it otherwise

BMS_SWREQ_ISOLATION_RATIO.content:
The isolation monitor component shall compute the isolation ratio as the
measured isolation resistance in ohms divided by the measured pack voltage in
volts, and shall report the ratio as invalid whenever the pack voltage is below
50 V. An invalid ratio carries no value a consumer may compare against a limit.
BMS_SWREQ_ISOLATION_RATIO.title: The isolation monitor component shall compute the isolation ratio as resistance over pack voltage and report it invalid below 50 V

BMS_SWREQ_LATCH_STATE_MACHINE.content:
The supervisor component shall enter the ``FAULT_LATCHED`` state on the first
limit-violation event and shall transition back to ``RUN`` only on receipt of
a diagnostic service reset request. While in ``FAULT_LATCHED`` it keeps
asserting the open command regardless of the values in subsequent sample sets.
BMS_SWREQ_LATCH_STATE_MACHINE.title: The supervisor component shall leave the FAULT_LATCHED state only on receipt of a diagnostic service reset

BMS_SWREQ_LIMIT_EVALUATION.content:
The supervisor component shall compare, once per 10 ms cycle, every sample of
the received sample set that carries a cleared invalid flag against the four
entries of the static limit table — undervoltage at 2.50 V, overvoltage at
4.25 V, overtemperature at 60 °C, and the debounced overcurrent condition —
and shall emit a limit-violation event naming the first entry that is
violated.
BMS_SWREQ_LIMIT_EVALUATION.title: The supervisor component shall evaluate every valid sample against the static limit table once per 10 ms cycle

BMS_SWREQ_LIMIT_MINIMUM.content:
The power limit component shall publish, as the permitted discharge power, the
smaller of the temperature-driven share and the actuator-driven share, where
the actuator-driven share is 30 % while the actuator interface reports an
unconfirmed request and 100 % otherwise.
BMS_SWREQ_LIMIT_MINIMUM.title: The power limit component shall publish the minimum of the temperature-driven and actuator-driven power limits

BMS_SWREQ_MODULE_MEDIAN_VALIDITY.content:
The acquisition component shall compute, per module and per cycle, the median
of that module's cell voltage samples, and shall set the invalid flag on every
sample of that module whose absolute difference from the median exceeds
250 mV. All other samples of the module carry a cleared invalid flag.
BMS_SWREQ_MODULE_MEDIAN_VALIDITY.title: The acquisition component shall mark a cell voltage sample invalid when it deviates from its module median by more than 250 mV

BMS_SWREQ_OCV_TABLE_LOOKUP.content:
The corrector component shall map a mean cell voltage to a state of charge by
locating the two adjacent table points that bracket the voltage and
interpolating linearly between their state-of-charge values. A voltage below
the first point yields 0 %, and a voltage above the last point yields 100 %.
BMS_SWREQ_OCV_TABLE_LOOKUP.title: The corrector component shall derive the state of charge from the mean cell voltage by linear interpolation in the 21-point open-circuit-voltage table

BMS_SWREQ_OVERCURRENT_DEBOUNCE.content:
The current monitor component shall report an overcurrent condition on its
output once its internal above-threshold timer, incremented by the 1 ms sample
period on every sample above 350 A in the discharge direction and reset to
zero on any sample at or below 350 A, has reached 100 ms. Until then the
output reports no overcurrent condition.
BMS_SWREQ_OVERCURRENT_DEBOUNCE.title: The current monitor component shall report an overcurrent condition only after the pack current has stayed above 350 A for 100 ms

BMS_SWREQ_REST_DETECTION.content:
The corrector component shall report a rest condition once its internal rest
timer, incremented by the tick period on every tick whose absolute current
sample is below 1 A and reset to zero on any tick at or above 1 A, has reached
1800 seconds. The reported condition clears on the next reset of that timer.
BMS_SWREQ_REST_DETECTION.title: The corrector component shall report a rest condition after the absolute pack current has stayed below 1 A for 30 minutes

BMS_SWREQ_SOC_PERSIST_WRITE.content:
The store component shall write one record — state of charge, write counter
incremented by one, and checksum over both — into the slot not used by the
previous write, on every shutdown request and additionally whenever 60 seconds
have passed since its last write. The slot it overwrites is always the one
carrying the lower write counter.
BMS_SWREQ_SOC_PERSIST_WRITE.title: The store component shall write the two-slot state-of-charge record on every shutdown request and every 60 seconds while awake

BMS_SWREQ_SOC_RESTORE_SLOT.content:
The store component shall, on initialisation, verify the checksum of both
slots and return the state of charge of whichever checksum-valid slot carries
the higher write counter. When neither slot is checksum-valid it reports that
no stored value is available.
BMS_SWREQ_SOC_RESTORE_SLOT.title: The store component shall restore the state of charge from the valid slot carrying the higher write counter

BMS_SWREQ_STATE_FRAME_PERIOD.content:
The publisher component shall send one battery state frame, carrying the last
values it holds for state of charge, remaining capacity and the validity
verdict, every 100 ms with a tolerance of 10 ms while the system is awake. A
producer that has not updated its value since the previous frame does not
delay or suppress the frame.
BMS_SWREQ_STATE_FRAME_PERIOD.title: The publisher component shall send the battery state frame every 100 ms

BMS_SWREQ_TEMP_DERATE_RAMP.content:
The power limit component shall compute the temperature-driven share of the
permitted discharge power as 100 % at or below 55 °C highest cell temperature,
as 0 % at or above 60 °C, and as the linear interpolation between those two
points in between.
BMS_SWREQ_TEMP_DERATE_RAMP.title: The power limit component shall compute the temperature-driven limit as a linear ramp from 100 % at 55 °C to 0 % at 60 °C

BMS_SWREQ_TEMP_EXTREMA.content:
The evaluator component shall publish, once per 100 ms cycle, the maximum, the
minimum and the difference between maximum and minimum of the cell temperature
samples that carry a cleared invalid flag. A cycle in which no valid sample is
present publishes no figures and reports the thermal picture as unavailable.
BMS_SWREQ_TEMP_EXTREMA.title: The evaluator component shall compute the highest, lowest and spread of the valid cell temperatures once per 100 ms cycle

BMS_US_CELL_BALANCING.content:
As a fleet operator, I want the battery pack to even out the charge between
its cells on its own, so that the usable capacity of the pack is not dragged
down by whichever single cell drifted furthest from the rest.

The capability is observable from the vehicle. After a charge session the
pack reports a cell voltage spread that has shrunk rather than grown. Over
months, the usable capacity of the pack tracks the average cell rather than
the weakest one, which the fleet report shows as a slower loss of range. A
workshop reading the per-cell voltages after a standing period sees them
converged into a narrow band instead of fanned out.

Out of scope for this story: protecting cells from damage, reporting
remaining charge, and regulating pack temperature. Those are separate
capabilities with their own stories.
BMS_US_CELL_BALANCING.title: Even out the charge across the cells so the pack keeps its usable capacity

BMS_US_CELL_PROTECTION.content:
As a vehicle safety engineer, I want the battery pack to remove itself from
the high-voltage circuit as soon as any cell leaves its safe voltage, current
or temperature window, so that no single cell is ever driven into a condition
that can start a thermal runaway.

The capability is observable from outside the pack. The driver sees a battery
warning and a loss of drive power. The workshop sees a stored fault entry
naming the cell and the limit it crossed. A test bench that forces a cell
past a limit measures the high-voltage terminals going dead within a bounded
reaction time. The pack stays disconnected until a qualified technician
clears the fault, so an intermittent condition cannot silently re-close the
circuit.

Out of scope for this story: how accurately the pack reports its remaining
charge, and how it regulates its own temperature during normal driving. Those
are separate capabilities with their own stories.
BMS_US_CELL_PROTECTION.title: Disconnect the high-voltage battery before any cell can be damaged

BMS_US_ISOLATION_MONITORING.content:
As a fleet operator, I want the battery management system to watch the
insulation between the high-voltage pack and the vehicle chassis, so that a
degrading isolation barrier is reported before anyone can touch a live part.

The capability is observable from the vehicle. The dashboard shows an isolation
fault, and the diagnostic interface reports the measured isolation resistance,
so a workshop can confirm the finding with a hand-held insulation tester.

Out of scope for this story: protecting cells from over-voltage or
over-temperature, and opening the contactors — those reactions belong to the
cell-protection story.
BMS_US_ISOLATION_MONITORING.title: Detect a loss of high-voltage isolation before it becomes a touch hazard

BMS_US_STATE_ESTIMATION.content:
As a fleet operator, I want the battery pack to report how much energy it has
left and how much of its original capacity it has lost, so that I can trust
the predicted range of a vehicle and plan when a pack needs replacing.

The capability is observable from the vehicle. The dashboard shows a charge
level that stays within a stated tolerance of the energy the vehicle actually
delivers before it stops. The level does not jump when the vehicle is
switched off and on again. The fleet report shows a remaining-capacity figure
that only decreases over the life of the pack. A workshop that fully
discharges and fully recharges a pack can confirm both figures against the
energy that physically went in and out.

Out of scope for this story: protecting the cells from damage, and regulating
pack temperature. Those are separate capabilities with their own stories.
BMS_US_STATE_ESTIMATION.title: Report a trustworthy remaining charge and remaining capacity for the pack

BMS_US_THERMAL_MANAGEMENT.content:
As a driver, I want the battery pack to warm itself when it is cold and cool
itself when it is hot, so that I get the charging speed I was promised and
the pack does not age faster than the warranty assumes.

The capability is observable from the vehicle. On a cold morning the
available charging power rises within a stated time instead of staying low
for the whole session. On a hot day the pack keeps delivering drive power at
a reduced but predictable level instead of cutting out. The workshop can read
back the cooling and heating requests the pack made together with the
temperatures that caused them. The temperature spread between the warmest and
the coldest cell stays inside a stated band, so no part of the pack ages
ahead of the rest.

Out of scope for this story: disconnecting the pack on a safety fault, and
reporting remaining charge. Those are separate capabilities with their own
stories.
BMS_US_THERMAL_MANAGEMENT.title: Keep the pack in its usable temperature band while driving and charging

DEC_BMS_AS_EXTERNAL_PRODUCT.content:
**Context:** The battery-electric products need the battery management
system (BMS), which is developed as a separate product with its own
requirements, variants (cell chemistry) and releases.

**Alternatives:** (1) Import the released BMS needs per chemistry as
external needs. (2) Mount the BMS documentation sources into the CV build.
(3) Copy the relevant BMS requirements into the CV documentation.

**Consequences:** The CV platform links to BMS interface needs only,
pins a BMS release and selects the chemistry per product; the traction
power manager allocates the BMS power derating. BMS pages are not part of
the CV documentation.

**Rationale:** Alternative 1 keeps the BMS independent and needs no BMS
configuration in the CV project; mounting would require the BMS
metamodel and variant data, copying would drift from the BMS.
DEC_BMS_AS_EXTERNAL_PRODUCT.title: Use the BMS as an external product

DEC_CHARGING_INLET_PRIORITY.content:
**Context:** The Kconfig model allows a product with both megawatt
charging (MCS) and a roof pantograph, but the vehicle has room for one
high-power charging interface.

**Alternatives:** (1) MCS first. (2) Pantograph first. (3) Forbid the
combination in Kconfig.

**Consequences:** The high-power charging interface is selected in the
order MCS, pantograph, none; a product with both features gets the MCS
interface and no pantograph requirement is satisfied.

**Rationale:** MCS serves long-haul trucks, the main BEV use case; the
order keeps the Kconfig model open for a future pantograph truck.
DEC_CHARGING_INLET_PRIORITY.title: MCS takes priority over the pantograph

IMPL_CHG_CURRENT_LIMIT.title: Charging current from power and pack voltage

IMPL_CHG_SESSION_START.title: Start session only with locked inlet

IMPL_VCU_HV_SHUTDOWN.title: Request contactor opening on isolation fault

REQ_ENERGY_SOURCE.content:
The vehicle shall display the remaining energy as the state of charge
reported by the battery management system, in percent with a resolution
of 1 %.
REQ_ENERGY_SOURCE.title: Remaining energy display

REQ_HV_SHUTDOWN_ON_ISOLATION_FAULT.content:
The vehicle shall open both poles of the high-voltage battery connection
within 100 ms after the battery management system sets the isolation
fault.
REQ_HV_SHUTDOWN_ON_ISOLATION_FAULT.title: High-voltage shutdown on isolation fault

REQ_MAX_CHARGE_POWER.content:
The vehicle shall accept an average charging power of at least the value of
this requirement while charging from 20 % to 80 % state of charge at a
battery temperature of 25 °C.
REQ_MAX_CHARGE_POWER.title: Maximum charging power

REQ_NA_CHARGING_STANDARD.content:
The vehicle shall provide a CCS1 (Combined Charging System, type 1)
charging inlet according to SAE J1772.
REQ_NA_CHARGING_STANDARD.title: North American charging standard

REQ_RANGE_ESTIMATE.content:
The vehicle shall display the estimated remaining range in kilometres with a
resolution of 1 km, calculated from the remaining energy and the average
consumption of the last 50 km (the nominal consumption until 50 km are
driven). Energy source of this product: :variant:`powertrain.type`.
REQ_RANGE_ESTIMATE.title: Range estimate

REQ_TRACTION_POWER_LIMIT.content:
The vehicle shall limit the traction power measured at the drive axle to the
value of this requirement, with a tolerance of 5 %.
REQ_TRACTION_POWER_LIMIT.title: Traction power limit

RISK_HV_EXPOSURE.content:
A failed insulation of the high-voltage system can expose the driver or a
workshop technician to a dangerous touch voltage.
RISK_HV_EXPOSURE.title: Electric shock after an insulation failure

SWREQ_CHG_CURRENT_LIMIT.content:
The CHG software shall request a charging current of at most the maximum
charging power divided by the nominal pack voltage of the product.
SWREQ_CHG_CURRENT_LIMIT.title: Limit charging current

SWREQ_CHG_INTERFACE_DERATING.content:
The CHG software shall halve the requested charging current while the
contact temperature of the charging interface exceeds 90 °C.
SWREQ_CHG_INTERFACE_DERATING.title: Derate on hot charging contacts

SWREQ_CHG_SESSION_START.content:
The CHG software shall start a charging session only while the CCS inlet is
reported as locked.
SWREQ_CHG_SESSION_START.title: Start session only with locked inlet

SWREQ_VCU_ENERGY_DISPLAY.content:
The VCU software shall send the remaining energy of the energy source to the
instrument cluster in percent, rounded to 1 %, once per second.
SWREQ_VCU_ENERGY_DISPLAY.title: Send remaining energy

SWREQ_VCU_HV_SHUTDOWN.content:
The VCU software shall send the contactor-open request to the BMS within
10 ms after receiving the isolation fault.
SWREQ_VCU_HV_SHUTDOWN.title: Request contactor opening on isolation fault

SWREQ_VCU_POWER_LIMIT_APPLY.content:
The VCU software shall limit the torque request to the active power limit
divided by the current motor speed.
SWREQ_VCU_POWER_LIMIT_APPLY.title: Apply traction power limit

TEST_CHG_CURRENT_LIMIT.title: Charging current follows the pack voltage

TEST_CHG_SESSION_START.title: Session starts only with locked inlet

TEST_VCU_ENERGY_DISPLAY.title: Remaining energy is rounded to percent

TEST_VCU_POWER_LIMIT_APPLY.title: Torque is limited by the power limit

US_FAST_DEPOT_CHARGING.content: As a fleet operator, I recharge a vehicle within a driver break.
US_FAST_DEPOT_CHARGING.title: Fast depot charging

US_HV_SAFETY.content:
As a driver, I see the high-voltage system switched off and a warning when
its insulation fails, so I am not exposed to electric shock.
US_HV_SAFETY.title: High-voltage safety

US_MARKET_CHARGING.content:
As a fleet operator, I charge the vehicle at the public charging
infrastructure of its market.
US_MARKET_CHARGING.title: Charging in the home market

US_PREDICTABLE_POWER.content: As a driver, I can rely on a known maximum traction power of my vehicle.
US_PREDICTABLE_POWER.title: Predictable traction power

US_RANGE_AWARENESS.content: As a driver, I know the remaining energy and range of my vehicle.
US_RANGE_AWARENESS.title: Range awareness

arch.description: Mapping of uml key to uml content.

chain_reqs.description: Requirement ids this test result is evidence for, via test -> swreq -> arch -> req.

chemistry.description: BMS: pack cell chemistry a chemistry-specific need is resolved for (NMC or LFP).

code_url.description: Remote URL of the code marker (codelinks). Nullable: the BMS export carries null.

content.description: The main content of the need.

doctype.description: The markup type of the content, denoted by the suffix of the source file, e.g. '.rst'.

external_url.description: URL of the need, if it is an external need.

gap_category.description: Which gate reported this gap: trace_backward, trace_forward, orphan, status_disallowed, ...

gap_link.description: The link name the reporting gate counted, when the gap is a trace gap; empty otherwise.

gap_need_id.description: Id of the need the gap is attributed to, as a field a report template can read.

gap_need_type.description: Type of the need the gap is attributed to, so a report can group gaps by V-model level.

gap_shortfall.description: How far short the need fell, as a label: "<have> of <need>" links present.

layout.description: Key of the layout, which is used to render the need.

outcome.description: Recorded outcome of one test case in one run: passed, failed, error or skipped.

parts.description: Mapping of parts, a.k.a. sub-needs, IDs to data that overrides the need's data

product.description: Product the evidence (test result, gap) belongs to; one of configs/*_defconfig.

runtime_s.description: Wall-clock runtime of that test case, in seconds, as the report recorded it.

status.description: Lifecycle state of an authored spec need: draft -> review -> approved; `imported` on every pinned BMS need.

style.description: Comma-separated list of CSS classes (all appended by `needs_style_`).

test_run_label.description: Identifier of the test run the outcome came from: the report's timestamp, as a label.

value.description: Product-specific value of a vehicle requirement, resolved per product (variant functions).
